sales.label: Sell in the year of the death

A.dtt_note: county only (0.11%); no city add-on identified - see F-11 note in the register
A.recording_note: $100 first page less the $10 fraud-fee offset when DTT applies, + $3 per additional page (4 pages assumed)

B.dtt_note: SF tier $3.75 per $500 applied to the whole consideration (a cliff, not a marginal rate)
B.recording_note: documents subject to SF transfer tax are exempt from the recording fee

rules.prop19_window: transfers 2026-02-16 through 2027-02-15 window is not yet published; current published amount $1,044,590 applies to transfers 2025-02-16 to 2027-02-15
prop19_requires: becomes the transferee's principal residence, and the transferee must apply for the homeowners' exemption within 1 year of the transfer
value cap = factored base year value + indexed $1,000,000; market value above the cap is added to the transferred base year value
claim form (BOE-19-P) filed within 3 years of the transfer or before transfer to a third party
rules.sc_rate_components_official: 1.00000% maximum tax levy + voter-approved bonds by tax rate area

laws.rule: Unified estate/gift tax; basic exclusion amount
laws.detail: Filing threshold by year of death, as published: 2024 $13,610,000; 2025 $13,990,000; 2026 $15,000,000. Top rate 40% above the threshold. Portability of the unused exclusion (DSUE) requires a timely Form 706.
laws.watch: Any bill changing the exclusion or the 40% rate. No pending measure was verified in this session - do not model one.

laws.rule: California estate tax / inheritance tax
laws.detail: This model assumes California imposes NO estate or inheritance tax. That is the conventional position and it matches the FTB materials reviewed, but no official source was read that states it in terms. Flagged (F-6) because it is load-bearing for the 'considerable cash' side of the plan.
laws.watch: Ask the CPA to put the 'no CA estate tax' conclusion in writing with a citation.

laws.rule: Basis step-up at death (IRC 1014)
laws.detail: Basis becomes fair market value at the date of death (or the alternate valuation date if elected and it lowers the estate tax). This is why a sale in the year of death usually produces little or no gain - and it has NOTHING to do with the property tax bill.
laws.watch: Repeal or limitation of the step-up has been proposed in past Congresses and never enacted; nothing verified as pending now.

laws.rule: Long-term capital gains rates + net investment income tax
laws.detail: 2025/2026 published bands 0% / 15% / 20%; the 20% band begins above $533,400 (single) / $600,050 (married filing jointly). Unrecaptured section 1250 gain on depreciation is capped at 25%. NIIT of 3.8% applies above modified AGI thresholds.
laws.watch: Watch the NIIT thresholds and any surtax proposal; the model adds 3.8% to gains.

laws.rule: No preferential rate for capital gains
laws.detail: FTB, verbatim position: 'California does not have a lower rate for capital gains. All capital gains are taxed as ordinary income.' This is why a $2.5M gain costs far more here than the federal tables suggest.
laws.watch: No change verified.

laws.rule: Mental/Behavioral Health Services Tax: 1% on taxable income over $1,000,000
laws.detail: Read as line 62 of the 2024 Form 540 booklet: 1% of the amount by which CA taxable income exceeds $1,000,000 reduced by certain credits. The threshold is NOT indexed. Applied in the model on top of the 12.3% top rate for every sale year in which a large gain is recognised.
laws.watch: Recheck with the 2026 booklet when posted; confirm whether the threshold indexes.

laws.rule: Section 121 principal-residence exclusion
laws.detail: $250,000 single / $500,000 married filing jointly of gain, requiring ownership AND use as principal residence for 2 of the last 5 years. Inherited property usually qualifies only if the heir moves in - which is why 'live first, sell later' is a separate path (P-04, P-09, P-11).
laws.watch: No change verified.

laws.rule: Depreciation of residential rental property: 27.5 years straight line, mid-month
laws.detail: Only the building (land excluded) is depreciable, and only while held for rent. Every dollar claimed reduces the gain on sale - the deferral is real, the bill is too. Modelled with a 75% building allocation, which is an assumption (F-7).
laws.watch: No change verified.

laws.rule: Proposition 13: acquisition base year, factored at CPI or 2%, whichever is lower
laws.detail: Reaffirmed in the county's FY 2025-26 rate book. The 2% cap is what the model uses for every future year, including high-inflation years - that is the conservative (low tax) side of the assumption for the 'keep' paths.
laws.watch: No change verified.

laws.rule: Proposition 19 parent-child exclusion, R&TC 63.2
laws.detail: New taxable value = prior factored base year value + any market value above (prior FBYV + indexed allowance). Published allowance: $1,000,000 -> $1,022,600 -> $1,044,590 for transfers 2025-02-16 to 2027-02-15, indexed biennially by the California FHFA house-price index. Conditions: prior principal residence, heir's principal residence, homeowners'-exemption claim within 1 year, BOE-19-P within 3 years. Income use (rental) voids it entirely.
laws.watch: Next allowance publication expected 2027-02-16; a restoration of the full exclusion for all property types has been proposed in the Legislature (Prop 15 lineage) and has not passed - do not model it.

laws.rule: County documentary transfer tax, R&TC 11911
laws.detail: $0.55 per $500 of consideration (0.11%), measured on the price EXCLUSIVE of debt that stays with the property. A city may add one-half of the county amount and the county credits it. No municipal add-on was identified in the FY 2025-26 compilation (F-11: confirm with escrow).
laws.watch: A gift or transfer at death is not a sale; counties rely on R&TC 11930 to exempt it. 11930's text was not read this session (F-10) - get escrow's written confirmation.

laws.rule: San Francisco real property transfer tax (cliff tiers per $500)
laws.detail: $2.50 up to $250k; $3.40 to $1M; $3.75 to $5M; $11.25 to $10M; $27.50 to $25M; $30.00 above. The tier applies to the ENTIRE consideration, so it is a cliff, not a marginal schedule - a 1% price move can cost thousands. Exemptions include transfer to spouse/domestic partner, gift, transfer at death, and reconveyance to a trust the grantor owns. Owner-occupied realty for a resident is capped at 3.75 (Admin Code 1108.6).
laws.watch: Proposition I (2026) would have redirected half of this tax to affordable housing; it FAILED, so the tier table stands.

laws.rule: Proposition H Muni parcel tax (multifamily)
laws.detail: Approved 2026-11-03 with 74.4% (245,712 yes / 84,456 no). Multifamily: $250 base for the first 5,000 sq ft plus $0.195 per additional sq ft, capped at $50,000; 15 years starting July 2027; results certified by 2026-12-03; first bills FY 2027-28. Landlords may pass through no more than 50%, capped at $65 per unit, only where the rent was set before 2027-06-01.
laws.watch: Certification is the only remaining step; after that it is a cost in every Property B path and must be re-read when the first bills issue.

laws.rule: Proposition RTM regional transit assessment (1 cent SF / half cent SCC)
laws.detail: Approved 2026-11-03; collection begins April 2027. It is a sales/use tax surcharge, so it raises the cost of every appliance, roof and repair in the capital plan rather than the property tax.
laws.watch: Confirm the start month before pricing the 5-year capital plan.

laws.rule: Measure S parcel fee (Safe, Clean Water and Flood Protection)
laws.detail: Approved November 2020, no expiry date, adjusts up to 2% a year, billed as a line on the property tax bill. This is the most likely reason the household's bills imply a rate above the county's 1% levy (F-2). Modelled as a separate $0 for now and flagged, because the per-parcel charge for this parcel was not read.
laws.watch: Read the district's current parcel-charge schedule and put the actual number here.

laws.rule: AB 1482 rent cap: 5% + CPI, maximum 10%; just-cause eviction
laws.detail: Used in the model only as an UPPER BOUND on assumed rent growth for covered units, and to justify a 5% vacancy/turn allowance. The statute text (Civ. Code 1947.12) was not read this session, and the local CPI ordinance for Santa Clara County was not obtained (F-3).
laws.expires: 2030-01-01 (an expiry is stated in the summaries; not verified)
laws.watch: The 2030 expiry is the single most consequential tenant-law date for the rent paths.

laws.rule: Owner move-in eviction, Rent Ordinance 37.9(a)(11) and 37.9C relocation
laws.detail: One owner-move-in per building; the heir must move in within 3 months and live there 36 continuous months; 25% ownership minimum; tenants aged 60+ with 10 years' tenancy (or catastrophically ill with 5) cannot be moved out of a 2+ unit building. Relocation per the latest table read: $7,910 per tenant, $23,730 per unit maximum, plus $5,280 for each elderly/disabled/minor household member with NO cap on the extras (notices served 2024-03-01 to 2025-02-28).
laws.watch: The 2025-03-01 onward schedule was not located - do not rely on the dollar amounts without re-reading the current Form 579 (F-4).

laws.rule: Change in ownership on sale of a leased property, R&TC 61
laws.detail: A transfer of the lessor's interest in a lease with a remaining term UNDER 35 years IS a change in ownership: selling Property B with tenants in place reassesses it in full. That is a property-tax consequence of the 'sell B' paths that most analyses miss.
laws.watch: No change verified.

laws.rule: Passive activity losses and the $25,000 allowance phase-out
laws.detail: The model treats rental losses as SUSPENDED rather than deductible against salary, and treats the real estate professional exception as unavailable. That is conservative for the rent paths. Phase-out runs from $100,000 to $150,000 modified AGI.
laws.watch: Have the CPA confirm the household's actual position; it changes the rent paths materially (F-13).

laws.rule: Like-kind exchange (IRC 1031) for rental property
laws.detail: Available only for property held for investment or business use - never for the principal residence, and never for Property A if the heir lives in it. Defers gain and carries the low basis forward; combined with a fresh Prop 13 base at the replacement property it can be the cheapest option, but it locks in illiquidity. Decision and written advice must be obtained BEFORE a sale (see Q-14).
laws.watch: Recurring proposals to limit or repeal 1031.
